rationale: Y directly engages the two threads the human reviewers cared about most — it explicitly validates that native-speed streaming is now scoped correctly across HTTP/SSE vs WebSocket, and that duration_factor bounds are consistent across adapter/talker/S2Mel — matching what the ground-truth comments and author's fix responses describe. X's review, while detailed and well-argued on its own terms (mel_head bias, S2Mel zero-audio path, IndexTTS-2 regression risk), never touches any of the ground-truth reviewers' core concerns (speed/streaming validation, bounds consistency, native-model validation evidence), so its recall is much lower. Both are grounded and actionable with concrete file:line citations, but Y's explicit validate/refute methodology (quoting exact code and confirming hypotheses) gives it a precision edge.
